findings.title: Materials' 59-point lens gap is a bet on 118% growth
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.61x forward against 36.24x trailing, a 59-point percentile gap that is the widest in the table. The market is underwriting 118 percent earnings growth, which would be an extraordinary reversion for a sector whose trailing multiple sits at the 87th percentile of its own five-year range.

findings.title: Energy's forward percentile collapsed while trailing stays rich
findings.body: Energy's forward multiple has fallen 22 percentile points in a month to the 38th percentile, yet its trailing P/E remains at the 84th percentile. That 45-point gap implies analysts expect 64 percent earnings growth, a sharp recovery that the market is pricing in despite the sector's recent slide.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' one-week surge is an outlier move
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile jumped 38 points in a single week, the largest weekly swing in the table, after a 49-point monthly gain. The forward multiple now sits at the 70th percentile while the trailing lens is even richer at the 84th, suggesting the re-rating is not just sentiment but a genuine upgrade in earnings expectations.
